rationale: The pain is real and recurring — indie SaaS operators and self-hosted infra owners genuinely pay for bandwidth consumed by bots, and the Cloudflare-independence signal suggests budget awareness. However, effective bot-filtering without centralized infrastructure is a hard technical problem that goes well beyond Claude prompts: it requires reverse-proxy logic, fingerprinting heuristics, and ongoing cat-and-mouse maintenance against evolving headless-browser bots — scoring low on both buildability and operational autonomy. The buyer is identifiable (indie SaaS operators, small eng teams) but the solution cannot be delivered or maintained hands-off, so the build gates on buildability_with_ai (4 vs floor of 6) and operational_autonomy (4 vs floor of 7) are both unmet.
solution_plan: This idea cannot realistically be built and run by a solo non-technical operator using Claude + this factory. Effective bot-filtering is an infrastructure security product requiring a reverse proxy, heuristic fingerprinting, and continuous adversarial updates — none of which are deliverable as a Claude prompt plus a landing page. Attempting to sell a Claude-backed wrapper here would produce an ineffective product and reputational harm. The factory could validate demand (draft an outreach email to indie SaaS founders on indie.hackers/HN, collect replies, map to existing paid tools), but should not attempt to build the product itself. Recommend a validate stage only: survey 20-30 target buyers to quantify their actual spend on bot damage and willingness to pay for a managed alternative, then re-evaluate if a credible technical partner or open-source core emerges.
notes: build_gate failures: buildability_with_ai=4 (floor 6), operational_autonomy=4 (floor 7). The core deliverable is a network-layer security tool, not an AI-wrapped workflow.
